The only interval in either Greek corpus given in days rather than centuries, and it is compulsory in both directions: seven days is how long a soul MAY stay and the eighth is when it must go. Between the thousand-year term and the choice of the next life there is a fixed recess, and it has a length.

rows.title_zh: 阄与择：责在择者，神无咎
rows.title_en: The lot and the choice: the blame is the chooser's
rows.text_zh: 《理想国》卷十 617d-618a。传令者宣告：「听命运女神拉刻西斯之言。必朽的灵魂啊，看哪，新一轮的生与死。你们的守护神不由分配给你们，而是你们选择你们的守护神；抽得第一阄者先选，他所选的生活便是他的命运。德性无主，人尊之则多得，慢之则少得；责任在于选择者——神是无咎的。」摆出的生活样式远多于在场的灵魂。
rows.text_en: Republic X 617d-618a. The Interpreter proclaimed: "Hear the word of Lachesis, the daughter of Necessity. Mortal souls, behold a new cycle of life and mortality. Your genius will not be allotted to you, but you will choose your genius; and let him who draws the first lot have the first choice, and the life which he chooses shall be his destiny. Virtue is free, and as a man honours or dishonours her he will have more or less of her; the responsibility is with the chooser — God is justified." And "there were many more lives than the souls present."
rows.display_title: 阄与择：责在择者，神无咎
rows.display_text: 《理想国》卷十 617d-618a。传令者宣告：「听命运女神拉刻西斯之言。必朽的灵魂啊，看哪，新一轮的生与死。你们的守护神不由分配给你们，而是你们选择你们的守护神；抽得第一阄者先选，他所选的生活便是他的命运。德性无主，人尊之则多得，慢之则少得；责任在于选择者——神是无咎的。」摆出的生活样式远多于在场的灵魂。
rows.source: Plato, Republic X 614b-621b — the myth of Er, in Benjamin Jowett's translation (Project Gutenberg #1497, public domain). Stephanus sections located against the Perseus canonical-greekLit XML (tlg0059.tlg030; Burnet's Greek, Clarendon 1905, and Shorey's Loeb translation, 1935-37, carry identical section milestones); Shorey's wording is not reproduced.
source_notes: Republic X 614b-621b describes a sentence being served, not a code of offences. This article is a rule of that process, which is why its polarity is PROCEDURE. GR-ER-04 is the one article in either Greek corpus that names wrongs, and it names three and then says 'any other'.

Gorgias covers this ground too and does not agree. Gorgias 526b-c stamps a soul and sends it to Tartarus or the Isles with no term and no return; the circuit, the tenfold rate and the rebirth are this dialogue's alone. Corpus GORGIAS holds that structure and no article here cites it.

αἰτία ἑλομένου· θεὸς ἀναίτιος — the load-bearing sentence of the whole myth, and the one that makes this cosmology's record meaningful. A soul's next life is not a sentence handed down; it is chosen, and the choosing is what it answers for. Cite this before attributing any Greek soul's condition to its disposition.

THE LOT DECIDES ORDER, NOT OUTCOME, and the myth closes the gap itself: there were more lives laid out than souls, so even the last to choose still chooses. An implementation that drew a Greek soul's next life at random would be citing this article against what it says.

THE CITATION SPANS TWO SECTIONS ON PURPOSE. The proclamation is 617d-e; the count of lives — 'far more numerous than the assembly' — is 618a. Jowett's prose runs them together and carries no section numbers, so citing the whole of it as 617d-e would put half the article at a reference that does not contain it. The remainder of 618a, and the catalogue of individual choices through 620d, are not transcribed.

rows.title_zh: 阿特洛波斯使之不可逆
rows.text_zh: 《理想国》卷十 620e。所选的生活经拉刻西斯与克洛托之手，再「带到阿特洛波斯那里，她纺出那线，使之不可逆转；此后他们头也不回地走过必然女神的宝座之下」。
rows.text_en: Republic X 620e. The chosen life passed from Lachesis and Clotho and was carried "to Atropos, who spun the threads and made them irreversible, whence without turning round they passed beneath the throne of Necessity."
rows.display_title: 阿特洛波斯使之不可逆
rows.display_text: 《理想国》卷十 620e。所选的生活经拉刻西斯与克洛托之手，再「带到阿特洛波斯那里，她纺出那线，使之不可逆转；此后他们头也不回地走过必然女神的宝座之下」。
rows.source: Plato, Republic X 614b-621b — the myth of Er, in Benjamin Jowett's translation (Project Gutenberg #1497, public domain). Stephanus sections located against the Perseus canonical-greekLit XML (tlg0059.tlg030; Burnet's Greek, Clarendon 1905, and Shorey's Loeb translation, 1935-37, carry identical section milestones); Shorey's wording is not reproduced.

The article that closes GR-ER-09. The choice is free and it is final in the same paragraph — freedom here is the freedom to choose once, not to revise. A Greek disposition is not amendable after this point, and the myth places the irreversibility with a named Fate rather than leaving it as an assumption.

rows.title_zh: 忘川平原与阿墨勒斯河：定量而非等量
rows.title_en: The plain of Forgetfulness and the river: a measure, not an equal one
rows.text_zh: 《理想国》卷十 621a-b。众魂「在灼热中行往忘川平原，那是不生树木草莱的荒野；傍晚在阿墨勒斯河边扎营，那河的水没有容器盛得住。他们都必须饮下一定的量，而那些没有被智慧所救的，饮得比必需的多；各人饮下便忘却一切。」
rows.text_en: Republic X 621a-b. The souls "marched on in a scorching heat to the plain of Forgetfulness, which was a barren waste destitute of trees and verdure; and then towards evening they encamped by the river of Unmindfulness, whose water no vessel can hold; of this they were all obliged to drink a certain quantity, and those who were not saved by wisdom drank more than was necessary. And each one as he drank forgot all things."
rows.display_title: 忘川平原与阿墨勒斯河：定量而非等量
rows.display_text: 《理想国》卷十 621a-b。众魂「在灼热中行往忘川平原，那是不生树木草莱的荒野；傍晚在阿墨勒斯河边扎营，那河的水没有容器盛得住。他们都必须饮下一定的量，而那些没有被智慧所救的，饮得比必需的多；各人饮下便忘却一切。」
rows.source: Plato, Republic X 614b-621b — the myth of Er, in Benjamin Jowett's translation (Project Gutenberg #1497, public domain). Stephanus sections located against the Perseus canonical-greekLit XML (tlg0059.tlg030; Burnet's Greek, Clarendon 1905, and Shorey's Loeb translation, 1935-37, carry identical section milestones); Shorey's wording is not reproduced.
source_notes: Republic X 614b-621b describes a sentence being served, not a code of offences. This article is a rule of that process, which is why its polarity is PROCEDURE. GR-ER-04 is the one article in either Greek corpus that names wrongs, and it names three and then says 'any other'.

Gorgias covers this ground too and does not agree. Gorgias 526b-c stamps a soul and sends it to Tartarus or the Isles with no term and no return; the circuit, the tenfold rate and the rebirth are this dialogue's alone. Corpus GORGIAS holds that structure and no article here cites it.

COMPULSORY BUT NOT UNIFORM, and that is the whole article. Every soul must drink a measure; the unwise drink past it. So how much a soul forgets is the last thing in the myth that still depends on what the soul is — after Atropos has made the life irreversible. `MemoryResetMechanism` records a mechanism per realm and has no room for a quantity, so this degree is NOT modelled anywhere and must not be read into the seeded value.

PLATO'S RIVER IS NOT LETHE. The PLAIN is Λήθης πεδίον and the river is Ἀμέλης, which Jowett renders 'Unmindfulness'; Shorey's note records that calling the river Lethe is later usage. The Greek realms carry `memory_reset_mechanism="LETHE"` because that is this system's enum member for the mechanism, not because Republic X names the river so.
Er himself was hindered from drinking, which is how there is a report at all. The exemption is narrative and is not a rule.

rows.content: 第一殿排队已到午门外,请勿喧哗。
Forty-two assessors on shift; bring your negative confessions in order.
孟婆汤新换了配方,说是少放了黄连。
今日当值第五殿,孽镜台前无人敢抬头。
Charon has raised the fare. Bring two obols.
The Ninth Circle's ice is holding nicely this season.
Minos asks everyone to stop counting his tail.
Sisyphus reports slight progress. It will not last.
Cerberus had all three breakfasts. Approach calmly.
The scales were recalibrated at dawn. Ammit is fed and resting.
Lethe is high this week; do not drink before your paperwork.
Boat of Ra departs at the twelfth hour sharp.
Limbo book club meets Thursday. Virgil is bringing the Aeneid, again.
崔判官的朱笔又断了,这是本月第三支。
奈何桥下水位上涨,诸位摆渡注意。
Purgatory's terraces are repainted; mind the fresh mortar.

Offsets involving such records are granularity-blind and may discharge a lump fault with scattered merit. This is why `granularity_applied` False does not by itself mean the rule was tested and did not bite.

b.name: 岔路草原
b.name_en: The Meadow at the Parting of the Ways

b.name: 夜游神
b.title: 夜游神
b.description: Patrols the living world by night and seizes wandering souls (docs/01 第五层; docs/02 §六) - the arrest side of the underworld, with 黑白无常
b.description_en: Patrols the living world by night and seizes wandering souls (docs/01 fifth layer; docs/02 §6) - the arrest side of the underworld, with The Impermanences

b.name: 孟婆
b.title: 孟婆
b.description: The Meng Po - keeps the 醧忘台 at the tenth court, 「居第十殿，冥王殿前六桥之外」, and serves the broth of forgetting to souls already sentenced and bound for the next life
b.description_en: Meng Po - keeps the Terrace of Forgetting at the tenth court, beyond the six bridges before the king's hall, and serves the broth of forgetting to souls already sentenced and bound for the next life

b.name: 日游神
b.title: 日游神
b.description: Patrols the living world by day and records good and evil (docs/01 第五层; docs/02 §六). CONDUIT with 黑白无常 as the least-wrong role: ActorRole has no term for patrol-and-record
b.description_en: Patrols the living world by day and records good and evil (docs/01 fifth layer; docs/02 §6). CONDUIT with The Impermanences as the least-wrong role: ActorRole has no term for patrol-and-record

b.name: 白无常
b.title: 白无常
b.description: White Impermanence (七爷 谢必安) - captures wandering souls, brings gentle death
b.description_en: White Impermanence (Seventh Master, Xie Bi'an) - captures wandering souls, brings gentle death

b.name: 黑无常
b.title: 黑无常
b.description: Black Impermanence (八爷 范无救) - captures wicked souls with chains of darkness
b.description_en: Black Impermanence (Eighth Master, Fan Wujiu) - captures wicked souls with chains of darkness

b.name: 钟馗
b.title: 钟馗
b.description: Demon queller - hunts malignant ghosts and wards the household (沈括 《梦溪笔谈·补笔谈》卷三; Dunhuang 《除夕钟馗驱傩文》). NOT A 《玉历宝钞》 FIGURE: he appears nowhere in that text and holds no office in the ten courts. His pairing with the 罚恶司 of the 四大判官 is a late popular attribution, and this row is filed at the fifth court for want of a posting, not on a source
b.description_en: Demon queller - hunts malignant ghosts and wards the household (Shen Kuo, Dream Pool Essays, Supplement, juan 3; the Dunhuang New Year's Eve exorcism text on Zhong Kui). NOT A JADE RECORDS FIGURE: he appears nowhere in that text and holds no office in the ten courts. His pairing with the Bureau of Punishing Evil of the Four Great Judges is a late popular attribution, and this row is filed at the fifth court for want of a posting, not on a source

b.name: 枷锁将军
b.title: 枷锁将军
b.description: Puts the cangue and chains on the dead so they cannot escape; has charge of the gravest offenders (docs/01 第五层; docs/02 §六). Custody rather than punishment, so GUARDIAN with 牛头马面
b.description_en: Puts the cangue and chains on the dead so they cannot escape; has charge of the gravest offenders (docs/01 fifth layer; docs/02 §6). Custody rather than punishment, so GUARDIAN with Ox Head and Horse Face

b.name: 牛头
b.title: 牛头马面
b.description: Ox Head - one of the two guardians who escort the dead. 《玉历》 names the pair at the fifth court, 「牛头、马面，押赴高台」, marching the condemned up the 望乡台; the escort itself runs across all ten courts
b.description_en: Ox Head - one of the two guardians who escort the dead. The Jade Records names the pair at the fifth court, marching the condemned up the Terrace for Viewing Home; the escort itself runs across all ten courts

b.name: 神荼
b.title: 东方鬼帝
b.description: Ghost Emperor of the East - holds 鬼门关 on 桃止山 and drives out malignant ghosts; with 郁垒 one of the two ancient door gods who bind ghosts with reed rope (docs/02 §二, which gives 《山海经》 as the earliest record). 鬼门关 is not modelled; filed at the holding pen, the nearest place before the first court
b.description_en: Ghost Emperor of the East - holds the Ghost Gate on Mount Taozhi and drives out malignant ghosts; with Yulei one of the two ancient door gods who bind ghosts with reed rope (docs/02 §2, which gives the Classic of Mountains and Seas as the earliest record). The Ghost Gate is not modelled; filed at the holding pen, the nearest place before the first court

b.name: 谛听
b.title: 谛听
b.description: 地藏王菩萨's mount - discerns true from false in a soul's testimony and helps deliver the dead; white, between dog and lion in form (docs/02 §一). A subordinate, not a deity in its own right, and a figure of Chinese folk tradition and 《西游记》, not of Buddhist scripture - the docs say so. Filed with 地藏 at the intake court. GUARDIAN is the least-wrong role: it decides nothing
b.description_en: Ksitigarbha's mount - discerns true from false in a soul's testimony and helps deliver the dead; white, between dog and lion in form (docs/02 §1). A subordinate, not a deity in its own right, and a figure of Chinese folk tradition and Journey to the West, not of Buddhist scripture - the docs say so. Filed with Ksitigarbha at the intake court. GUARDIAN is the least-wrong role: it decides nothing

b.name: 郁垒
b.title: 东方鬼帝
b.description: Ghost Emperor of the East - keeps 鬼门关 together with 神荼; the east is the one quarter with two emperors (docs/01 第二层; docs/02 §二). Placement as for 神荼
b.description_en: Ghost Emperor of the East - keeps the Ghost Gate together with Shentu; the east is the one quarter with two emperors (docs/01 second layer; docs/02 §2). Placement as for Shentu

b.name: 马面
b.title: 马面
b.description: Horse Face - companion guardian of the underworld dead; see 牛头 for the fifth-court 望乡台 escort 《玉历》 names them in
b.description_en: Horse Face - companion guardian of the underworld dead; see Ox Head for the fifth-court escort to the Terrace for Viewing Home that the Jade Records names them in

b.name: 五官王
b.title: 第四殿五官王
b.description: Fourth court judge - presides over 合大地狱: withholding grain tax and rent, fraud in trade
b.description_en: Fourth court judge - presides over the Great Crushing Hell: withholding grain tax and rent, fraud in trade

b.name: 判官
b.title: 判官
b.description: Judges who compile and verify the Book of Life and Death

b.name: 卞城王
b.title: 第六殿卞城王
b.description: Sixth court judge - presides over 大叫唤大地狱: sacrilege against images and scriptures, irreverence toward heaven and earth
b.description_en: Sixth court judge - presides over the Great Howling Hell: sacrilege against images and scriptures, irreverence toward heaven and earth

b.name: 宋帝王
b.title: 第三殿宋帝王
b.description: Third court judge - presides over 黑绳大地狱: defying one's elders, inciting litigation, betraying a trust
b.description_en: Third court judge - presides over the Great Black Rope Hell: defying one's elders, inciting litigation, betraying a trust

b.name: 崔府君
b.title: 崔判官
b.description: 崔珏 - senior registrar and judge of the underworld courts; keeps the Ledger of Life and Death and assists the Ten Kings
b.description_en: Cui Jue - senior registrar and judge of the underworld courts; keeps the Ledger of Life and Death and assists the Ten Kings

b.name: 平等王
b.title: 第九殿平等王
b.description: Ninth court judge - presides over 阿鼻大地狱, the deepest hell: murder, arson, poisoning, the gravest crimes
b.description_en: Ninth court judge - presides over Avici Hell, the deepest hell: murder, arson, poisoning, the gravest crimes

b.name: 楚江王
b.title: 第二殿楚江王
b.description: Second court judge - presides over 活大地狱, the mildest punishment court: abduction, appropriating what belongs to others, maiming
b.description_en: Second court judge - presides over the Great Reviving Hell, the mildest punishment court: abduction, appropriating what belongs to others, maiming

b.name: 泰山王
b.title: 第七殿泰山王
b.description: Seventh court judge - presides over 热恼大地狱: taking bones for medicine, and the scattering of kin from one another
b.description_en: Seventh court judge - presides over the Burning Hell: taking bones for medicine, and the scattering of kin from one another

b.name: 秦广王
b.title: 第一殿秦广王
b.description: First court judge - evaluates the Ledger of Life and Death

b.name: 转轮王
b.title: 第十殿转轮王
b.description: Tenth court - the wheel of rebirth; assigns fate for the next life

b.name: 都市王
b.title: 第八殿都市王
b.description: Eighth court judge - presides over 大热恼大地狱: unfilial conduct, the parent left unkept in life and unburied in death. 「都市」 is the capital, not a marketplace
b.description_en: Eighth court judge - presides over the Great Burning Hell: unfilial conduct, the parent left unkept in life and unburied in death. Dushi here is the capital, not a marketplace

b.name: 酆都大帝
b.title: 北阴酆都大帝
b.description: 北阴大帝 - head of the whole underworld from 罗酆山 (酆都城), superior of the ten kings in the Daoist pantheon; hears the last instance of an appeal
b.description_en: Great Emperor of the Northern Yin - head of the whole underworld from Mount Luofeng (the city of Fengdu), superior of the ten kings in the Daoist pantheon; hears the last instance of an appeal

b.name: 阎罗王
b.title: 第五殿阎罗王
b.description: Fifth court judge - the best-known of the ten kings. He sat at the first court and was demoted here for leniency, by his own account: 「吾本前居第一殿，因憐屈死，屢放還陽伸雪；降調司掌…叫喚大地獄、並十六誅心小地獄」. His court tries the intent behind the act, and the 望乡台 stands in it
b.description_en: Fifth court judge - the best-known of the ten kings. He sat at the first court and was demoted here for leniency, by his own account: out of pity for the wrongly dead he kept sending them back to life to clear their names, and was reassigned to the Howling Hell and its sixteen small hells of the heart. His court tries the intent behind the act, and the Terrace for Viewing Home stands in it

b.name: 陆判
b.title: 陆判官
b.description: Underworld judge of 《聊斋志异·陆判》, where the text calls him only 陆判 or 陆公 (the name 陆之道 is a later folk addition). This project's docs give him the 阴律司, revising the underworld's laws - an office with no source, absent from the 城隍 twenty-four bureaus (docs/02 §四)
b.description_en: Underworld judge of "Judge Lu" in Strange Tales from a Chinese Studio, where the text calls him only Judge Lu or Lord Lu (the name Lu Zhidao is a later folk addition). Popular lists of the Four Great Judges give him the Bureau of Underworld Law, revising the underworld's laws - an office with no source, absent from the City God's twenty-four bureaus (docs/02 §4)

b.name: 魏征
b.title: 察查司正堂
b.description: Head of the 察查司 - audits wrongful convictions and overturns a king's misjudgment; the opening node of the Chinese appeal workflow. 察查司 is this system's term, not a classical office: 魏征 appears in the underworld narrative of 《西游记》 ch. 10 as a living chancellor writing to 崔珏, not as a seated judge, and the popular four-registrar lists that do place him usually give him the 赏善司 instead
b.description_en: Head of the Bureau of Inquiry - audits wrongful convictions and overturns a king's misjudgment; the opening node of the Chinese appeal workflow. Bureau of Inquiry is this system's term, not a classical office: Wei Zheng appears in the underworld narrative of Journey to the West ch. 10 as a living chancellor writing to Cui Jue, not as a seated judge, and the popular four-registrar lists that do place him usually give him the Bureau of Rewarding Good instead

b.name: 东岳大帝
b.title: 东岳泰山天齐仁圣大帝
b.title_zh: 东岳泰山天齐仁圣大帝
b.description: 泰山神 - holds authority over the birth of all things and protects the souls going round the wheel of rebirth; very high in popular cult (docs/01 第一层; docs/02 §一.3). NOT 泰山王: the seventh court's king is a different seat, and that row's own note records that 《玉历》 does not give the seventh court Mount Tai. REALM IS A COMPROMISE: Mount Tai is not a modelled realm
b.description_en: God of Mount Tai - holds authority over the birth of all things and protects the souls going round the wheel of rebirth; very high in popular cult (docs/01 first layer; docs/02 §1.3). NOT King Taishan: the seventh court's king is a different seat, and that row's own note records that the Jade Records does not give the seventh court Mount Tai. REALM IS A COMPROMISE: Mount Tai is not a modelled realm

b.name: 后土
b.title: 后土皇地祇
b.description: 后土皇地祇 - source of both the living and the dead, keeper of birth, death and rebirth, of the earth and the underworld; one of the Daoist 四御, called 「大地之母」 and held to be the underworld's founder (docs/01 第一层; docs/02 §一.1). Above 酆都大帝 and 东岳大帝 in the docs' ordering. REALM IS A COMPROMISE: she has no seat this system models, so she is filed at the intake court beside 地藏王菩萨 and 酆都大帝
b.description_en: Sovereign Earth Goddess - source of both the living and the dead, keeper of birth, death and rebirth, of the earth and the underworld; one of the Four Sovereigns of Daoism, called Mother Earth and held to be the underworld's founder (docs/01 first layer; docs/02 §1.1). Above the Emperor of Fengdu and the Emperor of the Eastern Peak in the docs' ordering. REALM IS A COMPROMISE: she has no seat this system models, so she is filed at the intake court beside Ksitigarbha and the Emperor of Fengdu

b.name: 周文
b.title: 中央鬼帝
b.description: Ghost Emperor of the Centre - on 抱犊山, coordinates the other four quarters and keeps the balance of yin and yang (docs/02 §二). The docs record few sources for this seat and call its holder's name disputed. 抱犊山 is not modelled; filed at the holding pen
b.description_en: Ghost Emperor of the Centre - on Mount Baodu, coordinates the other four quarters and keeps the balance of yin and yang (docs/02 §2). The docs record few sources for this seat and call its holder's name disputed. Mount Baodu is not modelled; filed at the holding pen

b.name: 地藏王菩萨
b.title: 地藏王菩萨
b.description: Bodhisattva of the Great Vow - 地狱不空，誓不成佛. Delivers souls out of the hells; relief path for wrongful deaths and those in the torture chambers
b.description_en: Bodhisattva of the Great Vow, who will not become a Buddha until the hells are empty. Delivers souls out of the hells; relief path for wrongful deaths and those in the torture chambers

b.name: 张衡
b.title: 北方鬼帝
b.description: Ghost Emperor of the North - sits at 罗酆山 in 酆都 and keeps the underworld's punishments (docs/02 §二). The seat has a second candidate, 杨云; the docs list both. 罗酆山 is not modelled; filed at the holding pen
b.description_en: Ghost Emperor of the North - sits at Mount Luofeng in Fengdu and keeps the underworld's punishments (docs/02 §2). The seat has a second candidate, Yang Yun; the docs list both. Mount Luofeng is not modelled; filed at the holding pen

b.name: 杜子仁
b.title: 南方鬼帝
b.description: Ghost Emperor of the South - governs the southern ghost domain from 罗浮山 and subdues violent souls (docs/02 §二). 罗浮山 is not modelled; filed at the holding pen
b.description_en: Ghost Emperor of the South - governs the southern ghost domain from Mount Luofu and subdues violent souls (docs/02 §2). Mount Luofu is not modelled; filed at the holding pen

b.name: 赵文和
b.title: 西方鬼帝
b.description: Ghost Emperor of the West - governs the western ghost domain from 嶓冢山 (docs/02 §二). The seat has a second candidate, 王真人; the docs list both. 嶓冢山 is not modelled; filed at the holding pen
b.description_en: Ghost Emperor of the West - governs the western ghost domain from Mount Bozhong (docs/02 §2). The seat has a second candidate, Wang Zhenren; the docs list both. Mount Bozhong is not modelled; filed at the holding pen

b.name: Anubis
b.title: 掌秤者阿努比斯
b.description: Jackal-headed god - WORKS THE BALANCE. He tests the tongue of the scales and adjusts the plummet; the inscription over him in the Papyrus of Ani reads 'O weigher of righteousness, guide the balance that it may be stablished', and BD 30B calls him 'him who keepeth the scales'. He decides nothing. Cast CONDUIT: he leads the dead into the Hall and to the balance; ActorRole has no term for the one who operates the instrument

b.name: Horus
b.title: 引导者荷鲁斯
b.title_en: Horus - Who Leads the Vindicated Forward
b.description: Falcon-headed Horus son of Isis - takes the vindicated dead by the hand after the weighing and leads him forward to Osiris, lord of eternity (Budge, Papyrus of Ani, Plate IV; BM EA 9901/3, the Hunefer papyrus). He is not a gatekeeper of the Duat and he is not a prosecutor - the prosecution story belongs to the Contendings of Horus and Seth (Papyrus Chester Beatty I), a different text about a dispute among the living gods

b.name: Isis
b.title: 生命女神伊西斯
b.title_en: Isis - Goddess of Life and Magic
b.description: Great mother goddess - stands behind Osiris' throne in the Hall with Nephthys as he receives the dead (Budge, Papyrus of Ani, Plate IV). She was seeded into the Field of Reeds, which is where the acquitted go after the judgment she attends

b.name: Nephthys
b.title: 丧葬女神奈芙蒂斯
b.description: Protects the dead - stands with Isis behind Osiris' throne in the Hall (Budge, Papyrus of Ani, Plate IV). Same relocation and same reason as Isis

b.name: Ammit
b.title: 吞噬者阿米特
b.description: The Devourer - fore-part a crocodile, hind quarters a hippopotamus, middle a lion. She waits AT THE BALANCE in the Hall, which is where every standard vignette draws her (Budge, Papyrus of Ani, Plate III; BM EA 9901), and acts only if the heart fails. She was seeded into a realm named after her, which made annihilation look like an address she lived at; see EG_ANNIHILATION above

b.name: Ma'at
b.title: 真理与正义女神玛特
b.title_en: Ma'at - The Standard of the Weighing
b.description: Daughter of Ra - SHE IS THE STANDARD, NOT A JUDGE. Her feather is the counterweight the heart is weighed against, and she sits on the beam of the balance (BM EA 9901). The hall is named for her: wsxt nt mAaty, the broad hall of the Two Goddesses of What is Right, a dual. Cast GUARDIAN because ActorRole has no value meaning 'the criterion'; she was cast JUDGE, which seated the measure among the people applying it

b.name: Osiris
b.title: 冥王奥西里斯
b.description: God of the dead and resurrection - presides over the Hall of Two Truths, enthroned in his shrine, and receives the vindicated dead (Budge, Papyrus of Ani, Plate IV; BD 125A in the Papyrus of Nu, BM EA 10477)

b.name: Thoth
b.title: 书记之神托特
b.description: Ibis-headed god - THE REGISTRAR. He stands behind Anubis with reed-pen and palette, records the result of the weighing, and reads the finding to the assembled gods ('Hear ye this judgment...'); the Papyrus of Nebseni labels the ape on the beam 'Thoth, lord of the scales'. He reports the verdict; he does not pronounce it

b.title_en: Healing the sick by talisman, needle or medicine
b.text_zh: 以符法針藥救重疾一人為十功，小疾一人為五功，如受病家賄賂則無功，治邪一同。凡行治一度為一功，施藥一服為一功。

b.title_en: Rescue, pardon and mitigation of punishment
b.text_zh: 救一人刑死性命為百功，免死刑性命一人為百功，減死刑性命一人為五十功，救人徒刑為四十功，免人徒刑為三十功，減人徒刑為二十功，救人杖刑為十功，免人杖刑為八功，減人杖刑為六功，救人笞刑為五功，免人笞刑為四功，減人笞刑為三功。〔救謂非自己主事，得門竭力救之是也；免謂自己主事，特爽原免者是也。〕如依法定罪則無功，如私家減免婢僕之屬，同此論功。

b.text_zh: 誦念經典，漏一字為一過，漏一句為五過，音釋乖背，字音交差，一字為一過，念誦語句錯亂，有失文意，一句為五過，若念誦之時，心意不專為五過，邪婬雜想及思惡事為十過，住經語惡事訖續念經為十過，語常事為五過，接陪賓侶為三過，語善事為一過，不依誦經法式為五過，念經發嗔怒為十過，凌辱他人為十過。〔凡言十過，其功全無，並是虛念。但一過去功一分，十過去功十分，所以不用也。〕

b.description: No longer used (2026-10-29): an acquitted soul of Diyu goes straight to rebirth. Formerly: pure merit souls - highest bliss, for as long as the merit lasts; when it is spent the soul returns to the wheel
Souls awaiting reunion with loved ones. SOURCE UNKNOWN: no underworld place by this name appears in 《玉历宝钞》 or 《十王经》; treat as this project's own element until a source is produced
Intake court - the Ledger of Life and Death is read and the soul's case opened at the 孽镜台 (Mirror of Retribution); no punishment is administered here
活大地狱 - the mildest punishment court; thieves and those who wounded others in life
黑绳大地狱 - 忤逆尊长, 教唆兴讼, 背恩失节: defying one's elders, inciting litigation, betraying a trust
合大地狱 - fraud, withheld dues, falsified accounts
叫唤大地狱 and the 十六诛心小地狱 - the court that tries the intent behind the act: malice, ingratitude, envy, miserliness. The 望乡台 stands here
大叫唤大地狱 - sacrilege and irreverence
热恼大地狱 - taking bones for medicine, scattering of kin
大热恼大地狱 - unfilial conduct and betrayal of one's own house
阿鼻地狱 - the deepest hell; murder, arson, the crimes with no remedy
The wheel of rebirth - sentences are complete; the next life is assigned and the broth of forgetting drunk. No punishment is administered here
Souls awaiting judgment - held before the first court reads the ledger

Not a place and not a residence: the outcome recorded when the heart is heavier than the feather and Ammit devours it. Egyptian sources call this the second death — the person ceases to exist, is not punished, and does not go anywhere. Ammit is seeded in EG_HALL_TWO_TRUTHS, where she is drawn beside the balance (Budge, Papyrus of Ani, Plate III; BM EA 9901). The row keeps its primary key across the rename from EG_DEVOURER, so dispositions already recorded against it still resolve.
Egyptian paradise - eternal life in the Field of Reeds (inside or beyond the Duat is left open: docs/01 §2.1)

Entry to the underworld Duat, where the dead person's own passage west begins. What this row records is the start of a soul's journey and nothing else; the gates that passage then meets are seeded separately as EG_SEVEN_ARRWT and EG_TWENTYONE_SEBKHET, which carry their chapters and their edition.

b.name_en: The Seven Approaches to the House of Osiris
b.description: Book of the Dead 144 and 147, two variants of one text: 'knowing the names of the keepers of the seven approaches' — the ꜥrrwt-gates of the house of Osiris in the field of reeds. Seven gates, three keepers apiece (iry-ꜥꜣ doorkeeper, sꜣw watcher, smi herald), twenty-one named beings in all. Chapter title and counts from UCL Digital Egypt, Book of the Dead chapters by number (Quirke, 2002); the text is in Budge, The Book of the Dead: An English Translation of the Chapters, Hymns, etc., of the Theban Recension, vol. II — the volume already cited for the forty-two assessors' towns and clauses. This row is the set, not a member of it: no individual gate and no individual keeper is seeded, because no transcription of their names has been obtained and the order of the series has no second witness.
The weighing of the heart against Ma'at's feather

b.name_en: The Twenty-One Portals of the Field of Reeds
b.description: Book of the Dead 145 and 146, two variants of one text: 'start of the gateways of the Field of Reeds of the domain of Osiris' — the sbḫt-portals, twenty-one of them, one demon to each. A different series from the seven ꜥrrwt, in a different pair of chapters, and not a continuation of their numbering. Chapter titles from UCL Digital Egypt, Book of the Dead chapters by number (Quirke, 2002); the text is in Budge, Theban Recension, vol. II, the same volume the forty-two assessors come from. As with the seven, no individual portal and no individual demon is seeded: the names have not been transcribed here and inventing them is how this repository has gone wrong before.
Eternal paradise - the highest bliss realm in Christian tradition

The vestibule inside the gate of hell, before Acheron (Inferno III): the neutrals who lived without infamy and without praise, chasing a banner, stung by wasps and hornets. Outside the nine circles; Limbo is the first circle, not this.
Lustful souls - tossed by violent winds (Dante's Inferno)
Gluttons - lie in icy sludge beneath rain and hail
Avaricious and prodigal - push heavy weights (Dante)
Wrathful and sullen - fight on the Stygian marsh
Violent against neighbors, selves, God - in three rings
Fraud - ten concentric fosses of Malebolge
Traitors - frozen in the lake of Cocytus (Judas, Brutus)

The far bank of Acheron, where the dead are ferried in. Virgil, Aeneid 6.295-297 ('the way leads to that Tartarean stream of Acheron'); Dante puts Charon here too, before the first circle (Inferno III), which is why this is a threshold and not a circle. Euripides, Alcestis 252-256 has the same crossing as a lake. Not a destination: nobody is sentenced here.

Mount Purgatory entire: Ante-Purgatory (Purg. I-IX), the seven terraces and the Earthly Paradise at the summit, all of which are its sub-realms. Every soul admitted here is already saved; the suffering is remedial and it ends. The memory reset happens at the summit, in EU_EARTHLY_PARADISE after the seventh terrace — not on the way up

First terrace: pride. The penitent walks bent double beneath a great stone, past carved exempla of humility (Purg. X-XII). Love perverted. Pride has no circle in the Inferno at all — this is its only place in the poem

Second terrace: envy. The penitent's eyelids are sewn shut with iron wire (Purg. XIII-XV). Love perverted. Envy has no circle in the Inferno either; the withdrawn EU-DS-07 gave it an iron cage in the eighth circle, and no part of the poem contains one

Third terrace: wrath. The penitent walks through thick, blinding, choking smoke (Purg. XV-XVII). Love perverted. The Inferno's fifth circle also holds the wrathful, but it holds them as incontinence, not as one of the seven

Fourth terrace: sloth (acedia). The penitent runs without pause, calling out exempla of zeal (Purg. XVIII-XIX). Love defective — the single sin of too little love, and the hinge of the mountain. Sloth has no circle of its own in the Inferno: the accidiosi sunk under the Styx are read by some as acedia and by Dante as anger turned inward, and the reading is disputed

Fifth terrace: avarice, and prodigality with it. The penitent lies face down on the ground (Purg. XIX-XXII). Love excessive. Two directions of one disorder share the terrace, the same pairing the Inferno's fourth circle makes of the avaricious and the prodigal
Sixth terrace: gluttony. The penitent starves and thirsts beneath fruit trees whose scent draws and whose branches withhold (Purg. XXII-XXIV). Love excessive

Seventh and last terrace: lust. The penitent passes through a wall of flame (Purg. XXV-XXVII). Love excessive. What lies above is not an eighth terrace but the summit itself — the Earthly Paradise, Lethe and Eunoè, and the ascent to the stars

The summit of Mount Purgatory, above the seventh terrace: the garden of Eden, where Matelda keeps the two streams (Purg. XXVIII). A soul that has finished the seven terraces is drawn through Lethe, which takes away the memory of its sins (Purg. XXXI), and then through Eunoè, which gives back the memory of the good it did (Purg. XXXIII); after both it is 'pure and ready to rise to the stars'. This is the only place in the European cosmology where memory is touched at all — not the nine circles, where the damned remember everything, and not heaven, which a soul reaches already washed

Plato, Gorgias 524a: one of the two roads out of the meadow, taken by those who have lived justly. Pindar, Olympian 2 describes the same destination as requiring three lives without injustice on either side of the grave, with Rhadamanthys judging at Kronos' side — a harder entry condition than the Gorgias states, and one this row does not model. Not Homer's Elysian plain (Od. 4.563-568), which is an exemption from death granted to particular men rather than a reward for a life.

Plato, Gorgias 524a: the other road out of the meadow — that is what sends a soul here, and it is the half of this row Virgil does not touch. The place itself is Virgil's (Aeneid 6.549-556): walled three times about (6.549), ringed by the Phlegethon (6.551), its gate held by Tisiphone (6.555-556, sedens ... vestibulum exsomnis servat). What this row still refuses is Virgil's 6.566-569, where Rhadamanthus presides over it and scourges — because Rhadamanthus is seeded next door as a judge at the fork with Plato's division of labour, and one actor cannot hold both offices. That refusal is the basis rule doing its work rather than an exception to it: the contradiction is in the judgment, so Plato keeps it. Hesiod (Theogony 720ff) is a third account — the pit the Titans are imprisoned in, not a destination for human dead — and is not seeded.

Where the dead are ferried into the underworld, before any judging. Virgil, Aeneid 6.295-297 places the crossing on Acheron and 6.298-304 puts Charon at it; Euripides (Alcestis 252-256) has Charon summoning from the lake and Aristophanes (Frogs 180-270) has him rowing, so the ferryman is Greek and it is his position in the map that Virgil fixes. A separate EUROPEAN row, EU_ACHERON, carries Dante's crossing (Inferno III) with Dante's Charon on it — the same figure under a different poem, kept apart for the reason realms/0018 keeps Dante's Minos apart from Plato's. Nobody is sentenced here.

b.name_en: The Meadow at the Parting of the Ways
b.description: Plato, Gorgias 524a: the dead are judged in a meadow at the fork in the road, one way leading to the Isles of the Blessed and the other to Tartarus. This is a sorting point that stands BEFORE any punishment, which is the whole reason the three judges cannot be housed in a circle of Dante's hell. Both roads out of it are seeded, because the same sentence names them, and GR_ACHERON is the crossing a soul reaches it by — the one piece of the map that comes from Aeneid 6 rather than from this passage. See the basis note at the top of GREEK_REALMS.
